# A strict OC margin for proper critical BM-equality cap covers

This is a scoped three-fiber theorem. It does not assert that the
hypotheses hold for a general mixed-integer body or general critical
cap cover. Its proof needs no global homothety or cap-gluing theorem.

## Statement

Let d>=2. Let A,K,B be d-dimensional convex bodies with

    (A+B)/2 subset K,

and give the mixed set

    S=({-1} times A) union ({0} times K) union ({1} times B)

its d-dimensional Hausdorff measure, equivalently the sum of the three
d-dimensional fiber volumes. These can in particular be exactly the
nonempty integer fibers of any actual convex body. Write

    M=|A|+|K|+|B|,
    Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d.

Suppose a point y in K admits finitely many closed ambient halfspaces

    H_i={(z,x):u_i.(x-y)+alpha_i z>=0},  u_i!=0,

with all of the following properties:

1. Every H_i attains the raw halfspace depth at (0,y). Thus all have
   the same mass Q=inf{H_d(S intersect H):H a closed halfspace
   containing (0,y)}.
2. Both endpoint cuts are proper: each boundary plane meets the
   interior of A or B, respectively. Equivalently, each endpoint's
   captured part and strict complement have positive d-volume.
3. Each cap has exact captured-side Brunn--Minkowski equality:

       |K intersect (H_i)_0|^(1/d)
         = (|A intersect (H_i)_-1|^(1/d)
               +|B intersect (H_i)_1|^(1/d))/2.

4. The middle traces cover K:

       K subset union_i {x:u_i.(x-y)>=0}.

   In particular a positively balanced finite family of continuous
   normals has this property. Minimality or full rank of the circuit
   is not required.

Then the single deterministic mixed-integer point (0,y) has normalized
depth satisfying

    depth_S(0,y)
      >= 3 Gamma_d /
            [1+Gamma_d+((d+2)/(d+1))^d]
      > (3/5) Gamma_d
      > (1/2) Gamma_d.                              (1)

Thus this entire family has a strict margin over the n=1 OC constant.
The point need not maximize depth over all of S. No equal whole-fiber
volumes, no lattice width, and no symmetry are assumed.

## 1. A critical proper cap captures equal volumes in all three fibers

Fix an index i and abbreviate its continuous normal by u and integer
coefficient by alpha. Put

    F_D(t)=|D intersect {u.x>=t}|,
    sigma_D(t)=H_(d-1)(D intersect {u.x=t}).

At a proper level, the section area is positive and continuous;
Brunn--Minkowski makes its 1/(d-1)-power concave on the interior
projection interval. Fubini therefore gives

    F_D'(t)=-sigma_D(t)/|u|.

Changing alpha while keeping the source point and u fixed changes
the cap mass to

    F_A(u.y+alpha)+|K intersect {u.x>=u.y}|+F_B(u.y-alpha).

It has a minimum at the given alpha because this cap attains depth
at the fixed source point. Its derivative vanishes, so the two
endpoint sections have equal positive (d-1)-area.

The midpoint of the two captured endpoint bodies is contained in
the captured middle body: their thresholds average to u.y and
(A+B)/2 subset K. The assumed numerical equality, the ordinary
Brunn--Minkowski inequality, and equality of volumes in an inclusion
of full-dimensional convex bodies imply exact cap-set equality and
that the two endpoint cap bodies are positively homothetic. Write
their homothety ratio as lambda>0. Their artificial cut sections are
the respective minimum-u faces, hence have area ratio lambda^(d-1).
Equality of their positive section areas and d>=2 force lambda=1.

Consequently the two endpoint cap volumes are equal. The assumed
captured-side numerical equality gives the same volume for the
middle cap. Since their sum is Q, every one of these three volumes
is Q/3. This holds separately for every i. In particular all middle
cap volumes have the same value

    q=Q/3>0.                                        (2)

This argument also implies that the middle cuts are proper: choose
one point in each endpoint strictly below its own cut, and then one
point in each endpoint strictly above its own cut. Their respective
midpoints lie strictly on the two sides of the middle cut. Thus
q<|K|. No assertion that
the cap translations agree across different indices is needed.

## 2. The cover and the ordinary centroid give q>=Gamma_d |K|

Let g be the ordinary volume centroid of K. At least one middle
trace contains g by the assumed cover. The classical ordinary
Grunbaum theorem says that every closed halfspace containing this
centroid captures at least Gamma_d |K|. Applied to that trace, and
using (2), it gives

    q>=Gamma_d |K|.                                  (3)

This uses the centroid solely to certify a numerical volume bound.
The selected mixed-integer point remains (0,y). There is no rounding
or assertion that (0,g) is one of the critical sources.

## 3. Bound the whole-fiber mass using their roots

Put

    a=|A|^(1/d), c=|K|^(1/d), b=|B|^(1/d),
    k=q^(1/d), r=k/c.

Every endpoint contains one of its caps of volume q, so a,b>=k.
Whole-body Brunn--Minkowski and actual midpoint inclusion give

    a+b<=2c.                                        (4)

Properness and (3) imply

    d/(d+1)<=r<1.                                   (5)

For positive a,b>=k with a+b<=2c, monotonicity first allows the
sum constraint to be saturated by increasing either variable.
On the resulting interval a in [k,2c-k], the convex function
a^d+(2c-a)^d attains its maximum at an endpoint. Hence

    a^d+b^d<=k^d+(2c-k)^d,

and therefore

    M<=c^d [1+r^d+(2-r)^d].                          (6)

All powers here are the original d-dimensional volumes. No
projection integral or lower-dimensional counting surrogate enters.

## 4. Track the exact constant

Since Q=3q=3r^d c^d, (6) gives

    Q/M >= f_d(r):=3r^d/[1+r^d+(2-r)^d].            (7)

For 0<r<2, direct differentiation gives

    f_d'(r)
      = 3d r^(d-1) [1+2(2-r)^(d-1)]
           /[1+r^d+(2-r)^d]^2
      >0.

Using (5) in (7) gives precisely the first inequality of (1).
For the strict numerical margin, Gamma_d<1 and

    ((d+2)/(d+1))^d
      = sum_{j=0}^d binom(d,j)/(d+1)^j
      < sum_{j=0}^infinity 1/j!
      <3.

The final strict inequality follows, for example, from
j!>=2^(j-1) for j>=2, with strict inequality for j>=3, and summing
the corresponding geometric series. Thus the denominator in (1)
is strictly less than 5. Since Gamma_d>0, (1) follows.

For d=2 the displayed explicit bound is 12/29, while the n=1
OC constant is 2/9. No sharpness of the scoped bound 12/29 or its
general-d analogue is asserted.

## Scope and degeneracy audit

The set consists of exactly three positive d-dimensional fibers,
so its intrinsic Hausdorff dimension is d and its finite positive
measure is exactly M. Fiber separation makes the sum identity
literal. Every cap under discussion is an ambient closed halfspace;
its integer coefficient is arbitrary, and the derivative varies
that coefficient through actual oblique ambient halfspaces.
Proper continuous cuts carry no d-volume on their boundaries, so
their derivative formulas do not discard any relevant boundary mass.
The raw depth Q controls all closed ambient halfspaces by its
definition, not just the finite critical menu.

The theorem explicitly excludes d=1, where section-area stationarity
does not force a homothety ratio of one, and excludes zero-volume
endpoint fibers. It is not an assertion for q<d, for more than three
nonempty fibers, for cap covers with supporting/empty endpoint cuts,
or for caps lacking exact BM equality. Those are hypotheses requiring
new arguments in any application to general OC.
